commits.subject: net: fixed THttpMultiPartStream duplicated closing boundaries - fix #565
commits.body:
THttpMultiPartStream.Flush appended the closing --boundary-- lines on every
call, and THttpClientSocket.RequestInternal computed Content-Length: from
InStream.Size before its Seek(0, soBeginning) triggered another Flush: the
body sent was 22 bytes longer than announced, and the server parsed the
trailing boundary as the next request line (http.sys: 400 Invalid Verb).
Every retry - e.g. each round trip of the NTLM/Negotiate handshake - added
one more copy.

- Flush now appends the closing boundaries only once (fFlushed flag), so it
  is safe to call it any number of times
- Add*() after Flush raise EHttpSocket instead of producing a broken body
  (AddFile checks before opening the file)
- RequestInternal rewinds InStream before Content-Length: is computed, so
  Size is right even without an explicit Flush call
- tests: Flush/Seek idempotency and byte-exact re-read in
  TTestCoreBase.MultiPartDecoder; two keep-alive POST of the same stream
  (plus a never-flushed one) against THttpServer and THttpAsyncServer in
  TNetworkProtocols.DoHttpBodyDownload - both red before the fix
commits.author: Sven Harazim

+# AI Bootstrap Environment for Free Pascal and mORMot 2
+
+This directory contains bootstrap tooling for AI coding environments that need to build and test this repository's Free Pascal / mORMot 2 code.
+
+> **Path convention:** in this document, `boot/` means this repository's bootstrap directory. It is not the Linux system `/boot` partition.
+
+## Why this exists
+
+AI coding runtimes are often temporary and minimal. A new runtime may have Git, a shell, and a C compiler, but no Free Pascal Compiler (FPC), no mORMot 2 checkout, and no matching mORMot static libraries.
+
+That creates an important failure mode: an AI can review Pascal source code and suggest changes without ever compiling them.
+
+The bootstrap tooling in this directory gives an AI agent a reproducible way to create a usable FPC + mORMot 2 toolchain before modifying Pascal code. The intended workflow is:
+
+1. Bootstrap the compiler and mORMot dependencies.
+2. Use the generated compiler wrapper for this repository.
+3. Compile relevant changes.
+4. Run the project's tests or build commands when available.
+5. Do not treat static source inspection alone as sufficient validation.
+
+## Files
+
+### `bootstrap-fpc.sh`
+
+Bootstraps a Free Pascal + mORMot 2 development environment for an ephemeral Linux runtime.
+
+By default it:
+
+- installs the build prerequisites on Debian/Ubuntu-style systems;
+- uses the distribution FPC as a bootstrap compiler;
+- builds the FPC `fixes_3_2` branch, expected to report FPC 3.2.3;
+- installs that compiler into an isolated prefix;
+- finds an existing mORMot 2 checkout or clones one into a cache;
+- downloads the mORMot POSIX static archive;
+- verifies the static archive against mORMot's SHA-256 checksum;
+- creates a local `fpc` wrapper next to the bootstrap script;
+- performs a small mORMot compilation smoke test.
+
+The script is designed to be idempotent. A fresh runtime performs the complete bootstrap, while a persistent runtime can reuse already-installed and cached components.
+
+### `fpc`
+
+Generated by `bootstrap-fpc.sh`; it should normally **not** be committed.
+
+The wrapper invokes the bootstrapped FPC with the correct private FPC configuration, mORMot unit search paths, and matching static-library path. Using the wrapper also avoids accidentally mixing the custom compiler with a system-wide FPC configuration from another FPC version.
+
+Add it to `.gitignore`, for example:
+
+```gitignore
+/boot/fpc
+```
+
+## Usage
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```bash
+chmod +x boot/bootstrap-fpc.sh
+boot/bootstrap-fpc.sh
+```
+
+Verify the compiler:
+
+```bash
+boot/fpc -iV
+boot/fpc -iTP
+boot/fpc -iTO
+```
+
+Compile a Pascal program:
+
+```bash
+boot/fpc path/to/project.lpr
+```
+
+If the repository already has a build or test script, prefer that workflow and configure it to use `boot/fpc` where possible.
+
+## Recommended instruction for AI agents
+
+Repository/project instructions can contain the following rule:
+
+> Before working on Pascal or mORMot 2 code, run `boot/bootstrap-fpc.sh`. Compile all relevant changes with `boot/fpc` and fix compiler errors before giving the final answer. Do not rely only on static analysis. Prefer the repository's existing build and test scripts when available, using `boot/fpc` as the FPC compiler.
+
+This instruction is intentionally written so it can be used with ChatGPT, coding agents, CI-like sandboxes, or other AI development environments that provide a Linux shell.
+
+An AI agent should not assume that a compiler installed during an earlier conversation or runtime still exists. It should check or rerun the bootstrap when entering a fresh environment.
+
+## Useful environment overrides

+| `FPC_EXPECTED_VERSION` | Version expected after the FPC build. Default: `3.2.3`. |
+| `FPC_PREFIX`

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Bootstrap a Free Pascal + mORMot 2 toolchain for ephemeral Linux runtimes.
+#
+# Intended location in your repository:
+#   tools/bootstrap-fpc.sh
+#
+# What it does:
+#   1. Installs the Debian/Ubuntu build prerequisites (including a bootstrap FPC).
+#   2. Builds FPC fixes_3_2 (currently reports 3.2.3) into an isolated prefix.
+#   3. Finds an existing mORMot 2 checkout, or clones one into the user cache.
+#   4. Downloads mORMot's POSIX static archive and verifies its SHA-256 checksum.
+#   5. Generates tools/fpc, a wrapper with the right FPC config, mORMot unit paths,
+#      and target-specific static-library path.
+#   6. Smoke-compiles a tiny mORMot program.
+#
+# Useful overrides:
+#   FPC_REF=fixes_3_2                 FPC branch or tag to build
+#   FPC_PREFIX=/some/path             FPC installation prefix
+#   FPC_CACHE_DIR=/some/path          download/source cache
+#   FPC_REFRESH=1                     refresh/rebuild even if already installed
+#   FPC_JOBS=4                        parallel build jobs
+#   MORMOT2_DIR=/path/to/mORMot2      use this mORMot checkout
+#   MORMOT2_REF=master                branch/tag used only when cloning mORMot
+#   MORMOT2_STATIC_URL=https://...    matching mormot2static.tgz archive
+#   MORMOT2_SKIP_STATIC=1             don't download static object files
+#   MORMOT2_SKIP_SMOKE_TEST=1         don't run the final mORMot compile test
+#
+# This script is intentionally idempotent. In a fresh ChatGPT runtime it will do
+# the full bootstrap; in a persistent environment it reuses the installed/cache
+# artifacts unless FPC_REFRESH=1 is set.
+
+set -Eeuo pipefail
+
+log()  { printf '\n[bootstrap-fpc] %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
+warn() { printf '\n[bootstrap-fpc] WARNING: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

commits.subject: net: fix lost thread wakeup in TAsyncConnections.ThreadPollingWakeupOne/Events
commits.body:
Since 73cb95431 the R1..Rn atpReadPending threads are woken up through two
CAS counters (fWakeupOne/fWakeupEvents) consumed by ThreadPollingWakeupLocked,
which is entered only after a successful fWakeupSafe.TryLock.

If a caller increments a counter just after the current lock holder did its
LockedGet32() and then fails its own TryLock, nobody consumes that request:
fWakeupOne stays at 1, so every further ThreadPollingWakeupOne() fails its
"if not already notified" CAS and returns without doing anything. On an idle
server this is fatal: the R0 atpReadPoll thread sleeps in WaitForEver (no
subscribed connection) or polls epoll forever (accepted connections are not
subscribed before their first read), accept() keeps succeeding but the new
connections are never processed - the process is alive but the HTTP server
is dead, with CLOSE-WAIT sockets piling up.

Observed on production RK3588 boards (THttpAsyncServer, 8 threads) after
8-18 hours, and reproduced in about 4 minutes (114 rounds) with a mix of
concurrent short-lived and keep-alive connections separated by idle gaps:
/proc stacks showed R0 in TSynEvent.WaitFor(INFINITE) from DoExecute and R1
idle in WaitForEver, with no runnable thread.

Fix:
- ThreadPollingWakeupLocked: after UnLock, re-check both counters and run
  once more if any is non-zero and the lock can be re-acquired, so a request
  raced against the holder is never left pending.
- ThreadPollingWakeupOne: always attempt the TryLock, even when fWakeupOne
  was already set, so a pending notification is self-healing on the next
  accept() instead of silently disabling all further wakeups.

With this change the same stress ran 1910 rounds / 45 minutes without any
stall (and 1160 rounds in a first 28 minutes run), where the previous code
died at round 114.
commits.author: zen010101

   // wake up one thread after accept() on idle server or on slow REST process

     fThreadPollingLastWakeUpTix := mormot.core.os.GetTickCount64; // 16ms / 4ms
-  if LockedExc32(fWakeupOne, 1, 0) then // if not already notified
-    if fWakeupSafe.TryLock then
-      ThreadPollingWakeupLocked; // only a single thread does the wakeup
+  LockedExc32(fWakeupOne, 1, 0); // notify (idempotent if already notified)
+  // always try to do the wakeup ourselves, even if fWakeupOne was already
+  // set: a previous notification may have been left pending by a caller

 end;
